---
title: "QA test users"
description: "Provision disposable signed-in test accounts for agent-driven QA with ttr qa users, mint automation sessions, and rely on automatic expiry cleanup."
updatedAt: "2026-11-20"
---

`ttr qa users` gives agents real, signed-in accounts in a deployed environment
(for example a Meet rehearsal with one staff host and 40 participants) without
touching real users. Every account is disposable: it carries an immutable test
marker, a reserved address, a run expiry, and is deleted automatically.

## Accounts

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Address | `qa+<run>-<n>@tutur3u.com` (participants) or `qa+<run>-<n>@tuturuuu.com` (`--staff` hosts) |
| Marker | `app_metadata.qa_test = true`, plus `qa_run`, `qa_owner`, `qa_purpose`, `qa_expires_at`, `qa_staff` |
| Run | 8-character ID; one operator, one purpose, one expiry (15 minutes to 72 hours) |
| Limits | 50 accounts per call, 200 per run, 5 staff hosts per run, 300 live and 600 created per 24 hours overall |
| Onboarding | Completed at creation, so automation lands on the app |

The database (`private.qa_test_users` and the `guard_qa_test_auth` trigger)
refuses any `qa_*` marker change, any address change, any signup that claims a
reserved address, and any attempt to add the marker to an existing account.
Deletion re-checks the marker and the reserved address before anything is
removed, so the QA path cannot delete a real account. The migration refuses to
apply while any existing account already uses a reserved address or marker.

QA accounts never verify as staff, including `--staff` hosts on the staff
domain: `isVerifiedTuturuuuStaffSession` and `private.staff_identity_verified`
return false for any marked account, so staff-only surfaces (support inbox,
short links, staff workspace secrets, domain entitlements, Mira and mail
tools) stay closed. Meet hosting is the one explicit exception:
`canVerifiedAccountHostMeeting` admits a `--staff` QA host until its run
expires. Give hosts `--tier pro` so meetings get paid-tier capacity. A QA
account can never join the root workspace, hold a platform role or allowance,
change its Auth role, or operate this API.

### Test tiers

`--tier plus|pro` grants the tier through the normal entitlement row
(`public.workspace_subscriptions`, status `active`) on the account's personal
workspace and on the run workspace. The row's provider ID uses the reserved
`qa_test_` prefix and is registered in `private.qa_test_subscriptions`; no
billing provider object exists, so checkout, invoices, seat billing and revenue
reporting never include it. Billing tools that reconcile with the provider skip
`qa_test_` rows. Deleting the account cancels its test subscriptions.

### Run workspace

`--workspace` creates one shared workspace for the run, named
`[QA] <purpose> <run>`. The first activated account owns it, so create the host
first, then append participants with `--run`. Every account in the run joins it.
It is deleted with the run's last account. Personal workspaces cannot be
deleted; they keep the same retained state as an ordinary account deletion.

## Operators

The API under `/api/v1/admin/qa/test-users` admits verified staff sessions that
hold `manage_qa_test_users` in the root workspace. Root administrators hold it
implicitly; grant it to a dedicated QA-operator role for anyone else. The CLI
uses the `ttr login` session.

## Commands

```bash
# Staff host with a Pro test tier and a shared run workspace (24 hours).
ttr qa users create --count 1 --staff --tier pro --purpose meet-rehearsal --ttl 24h --workspace

# 40 participants in the same run.
ttr qa users create --count 40 --run <run>

ttr qa users list [--run <run>] [--include-deleted] [--json]

# Playwright storage state (default) or raw tokens, written 0600.
ttr qa users session <userId> [--origin https://meet.tuturuuu.com] [--format storage-state|tokens] [--out <path>]

ttr qa users delete <userId>
ttr qa users cleanup --run <run>
ttr qa users cleanup --expired
```

Passwords, cookies and tokens are never printed or returned in `--json`
output. Passwords go to the macOS Keychain (service `tuturuuu-qa`, account =
address) or, elsewhere or with `--password-store file`, to
`~/.tuturuuu/qa/<run>/credentials.json`. Sessions go to
`~/.tuturuuu/qa/<run>/<userId>.storage-state.json` (or `.tokens.json`).
Directories are `0700`, files `0600`, and symlinked targets are refused.
`TUTURUUU_QA_HOME` overrides the root for tests. Delete and cleanup remove the
local files and Keychain items of deleted accounts.

### When every account fails

If no account is created, the API answers 503 with the run ID and, for each
failed account, the step that failed (`auth_create`, `onboarding` or
`activate`) and its rollback state. `ttr qa users create` prints them and exits
non-zero; the failed step is also in the server log. A `cleanup: pending`
account is retried by `ttr qa users cleanup --run <id>`.

### Sessions

`session` mints a fresh session without the password: the server generates a
magic-link token (no email is sent), verifies it, and returns the Supabase
session cookies for the requested origin. The origin must share the
deployment's session cookie scope (for example any `https://*.tuturuuu.com` app
when called on `tuturuuu.com`); this sets cookie attributes only, because the
session tokens work from any client. The request must be JSON. Every mint is
audited. A session lives until the run expires, when cleanup bans the account
(so refresh stops even if the delete has to be retried) and then deletes it;
delete the account earlier to revoke sooner.

```ts
// Playwright
const context = await browser.newContext({
  storageState: `${process.env.HOME}/.tuturuuu/qa/<run>/<userId>.storage-state.json`,
});
```

## Expiry cleanup

Cron Control job `qa-test-user-cleanup` runs every 15 minutes as a native
Cloudflare Worker processor (`apps/cron-control/src/processors/qa-test-user-cleanup.ts`).
It calls the ledger RPCs and the Auth admin API with the service key; no web
route is involved. Each slot lists at most 25 expired accounts and deletes them
one at a time within a 90-second deadline. The ledger leases each deletion for
10 minutes. The Worker removes the run workspace with its last account and
records that before the account settles, bans then deletes the Auth account,
and settles only after Auth reports it absent. The cleanup fence is checked
when each deletion begins and the Cron Control fence before every destructive
request. A refused step leaves the lease to lapse and fails the slot; an
unconfirmed write ends the slot as unknown before another deletion starts. A
later slot re-verifies either; nothing is replayed blindly. Repeated failures
trip Cron Control's consecutive-failure stop.

The Worker does not run Meet attendance subject erasure. Attendance rows of
these synthetic accounts age out through attendance retention.
`ttr qa users cleanup` uses the web operator path, which erases them
immediately; run it when a QA pass ends.

| Stop | How |
| --- | --- |
| Pause cleanup | `update private.qa_test_user_control set cleanup_enabled = false` |
| Pause provisioning | `update private.qa_test_user_control set provisioning_enabled = false` |
| Stop the schedule | Cron Control operator `stop` for `qa-test-user-cleanup`, or remove it from `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` |

The job is off until `qa-test-user-cleanup` is listed in
`CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`. Until then, run `ttr qa users cleanup --expired`
after each run: Auth does not expire the accounts by itself.

## Audit

`private.qa_test_user_events` records `create`, `session`, `delete`,
`workspace_create` and `workspace_delete` with the actor (`operator` with user
ID, or `cron`), run and account. It holds IDs, tier, purpose and timestamps
only.

## Regression coverage

- `apps/database/supabase/tests/qa-test-users.sql`: reserved addresses, marker
  immutability, the Auth insert-then-update ordering, staff exclusion, root and
  platform-role confinement, tier grants, leased deletion, stop fence.
- Auth admin ordering is verified once against the local Auth server: reserve,
  `auth/v1/admin/users` create, activate, magic-link verify, ban (refresh
  refused), workspace and account delete, settle.
- `apps/web/src/lib/qa-test-users/*.test.ts` and the route tests under
  `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/admin/qa/test-users/`.
- `apps/cron-control/src/processors/qa-test-user-cleanup.test.ts`: fences,
  request order, leased unknown outcomes, key headers. The processor was also
  run once against the local Supabase and Auth stack.
- `packages/sdk/src/cli/qa-users.test.ts`: secret handling and file modes.
